a.name: Wooden piece tap
a.desc: A tiny wooden game piece nudged on a board.
a.note: Chess piece set on a wooden board (close mic, raw take at 35.68 s: clean single contact with a short woody ring), pitched up 3 st so it stays tiny. Wood family with confirm a and cancel a.

b.name: Dry stone click
b.desc: A tiny dry click of stone on stone.

c.name: Old clock tick
c.desc: One soft tick from an old wind-up clock.
c.note: Single clock tick (mechanism, 2 ms rise), cut short and low-passed at 7 kHz so it is not sharp on repeat. Mechanism family with confirm c (gate latch) and cancel c (door latch).

a.name: Rising wooden tap-tap
a.desc: Two quick wooden taps, the second one higher, like a nod.
a.note: Board piece placement (firm wooden knock), then the same knock 5 st higher 60 ms later and 3 dB down: a rising 'tok-tik' that reads as yes. Bigger take on move a.

b.name: Stone tap, small bell
b.desc: A stone knock that rings a small, old bell.
b.note: One clean rock-on-rock hit (Rocks - hits, 38.06 s) gives the instant attack; a small glass bell ding pitched down 7 st and low-passed at 4 kHz rings under it, warm and old, not a phone chime.

c.name: Iron gate latch
c.desc: An iron gate latch lifting: clack, then a small click.
c.note: Gate latch (dense iron clack, cut 7 ms in so the peak lands early) followed 55 ms later by the Kenney RPG metal latch pitched up 3 st, 8 dB down. Bigger take on move c.

a.name: Low wooden tock
a.desc: A soft, low knock on a wooden table.
a.note: Kenney wood impact (medium), pitched down 2 st and low-passed at 3 kHz: one dull tock, lower and softer than confirm a.

b.name: Stone block set back
b.desc: Small stones clatter as a block is set down.
b.note: Two large cobblestone blocks (raw take at 12.02 s): a knock followed by a short stone rub. Pitched down 2 st, low-passed at 4 kHz. Lower than confirm b, no bell.

layers.credit: "two large cobblestone blocks" by jobel0092, CC0, https://freesound.org/people/jobel0092/sounds/268055

c.name: Door latch shuts
c.desc: A wooden door pushed shut, its latch clicking, muffled.
c.note: Kenney RPG door close, cut at the moment it meets the frame (195 ms) so the peak is early; pitched down 3 st and low-passed at 2.5 kHz so it is soft and lower than the gate latch of confirm c.

a.name: Heavy book opens
a.desc: A thick leather book cover thumping open.
a.note: Kenney RPG book open, cut in just before the cover lands (45 ms) so the thump peaks early; a page-turn rustle trails underneath at -12 dB.

b.name: Page flipped over
b.desc: A big old page turned over with a soft rustle.
b.note: Page turn (fs-397550), cut at the flip so it starts at once, pitched down 3 st to sound like a heavy parchment page.

c.name: Wooden lid creaks open
c.desc: An old wooden lid or cabinet door creaking open.
c.note: SFXWoodenObjectOpen raw take, cut at the first knock of the lid so the peak is early, then the wood creak tail.

a.name: Hardwood claves
a.desc: Two hardwood sticks struck: a bright, sharp clack.
a.note: Claves, single hit, 1.1 ms rise in the source. Cut to 60 ms so beats never smear.

b.name: Deep hollow woodblock
b.desc: A hollow wooden block knocked once, deeper and rounder.
b.note: Woodblock (medium), pitched down 3 st (tone near 1.5 kHz) so it sits clearly below the claves; cut 1 ms in to skip the soft first half-cycle so the peak comes at once; 60 ms.

c.name: Tiny timer tick
c.desc: A tiny, dry tick from a wind-up timer.
c.note: Ticking timer, one tick, cut 4.6 ms in to skip the soft pre-click so the peak is right at the start; about 26 ms, the shortest and driest of the three.

a.name: Stumble and thud
a.desc: A foot slams down hard, then boots scuffle in the dirt.
a.note: FX_The_Gilligan_Stumble raw take: the dull body thud (3.545 s) leads, a slice of its earlier shuffle (2.06 to 2.30 s) follows 40 ms later as the scuffle tail, low-passed at 6 kHz.

b.name: Shoulder bump
b.desc: A dull bump and a cloth rustle: the way out is blocked.

c.name: Thrown to the ground
c.desc: The hero lands hard on the ground, gear rattling.
c.note: soft heavy impact plus leather and buckle
